name: John Farnham
description:
'''John Peter Farnham''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|size=100%|AO}} (born 1 July 1949) is a British-born Australian singer. He was a [[Teen idol|teen pop idol]], billed as '''Johnny Farnham''' from 1967 to 1979. Farnham subsequently forged a career as an [[Adult contemporary music|adult contemporary]] singer. He mostly performed as a solo artist, although he replaced [[Glenn Shorrock]] as lead singer of [[Little River Band]] from 1982 to 1986. In November 1986, his solo single "[[You're the Voice]]" peaked at No. 1 on the [[Kent Music Report|Australian singles charts]]. The associated album, ''[[Whispering Jack]]'', held the number-one position for a total of 25 weeks. Both the single and the album had international top-ten chart success, including the album at No. 6 in the United Kingdom and No. 1 in Sweden. ''Whispering Jack'' is the [[List of best-selling albums in Australia|third-highest-selling album in Australian history]] and {{as of |May 2023|lc=yes}} remains the highest-selling album in Australia by any Australian artist.

Farnham became one of his country's best-known and most popular performers and is the only Australian artist to have a number-one record (album or single) in six consecutive decades (echoing the achievement of [[Cliff Richard]] in the UK), with singles including "[[Sadie (The Cleaning Lady)]]" (1967), "[[Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head]]" (1970) and "[[Age of Reason (song)|Age of Reason]]" (1988) and albums ''Whispering Jack'' (1986), ''[[Age of Reason (album)|Age of Reason]]'' (1988), ''[[Chain Reaction (John Farnham album)|Chain Reaction]]'' (1990), ''[[Then Again (John Farnham album)|Then Again...]]'' (1993), ''[[33⅓ (album)|33⅓]]'' (2000), ''[[The Last Time (album)|The Last Time]]'' (2002) and ''[[Two Strong Hearts Live]]'' (2015). He has toured with numerous artists, including [[the Seekers]] and international acts [[Stevie Nicks]] and [[Lionel Richie]]. He released collaborative albums with Tom Jones on ''[[John Farnham & Tom Jones – Together in Concert|Together in Concert]]'' (2005), Olivia Newton-John on ''[[Highlights from The Main Event]]'' (1998), ''Highlights from Two Strong Hearts'' (2015) and ''[[Friends for Christmas]]'' (2016).

Farnham has been recognised by [[List of awards and nominations received by John Farnham|many honours and awards]], including 1987 [[Australian of the Year]], 1996 Officer of the Order of Australia, and 22 [[ARIA Music Awards]], including his 2003 induction into their [[ARIA Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]]. Starting in 1969, he was voted by ''[[TV Week]]'' readers as the '[[Australian pop music awards#1967–1978: King of Pop Awards|King of Pop]]' for five consecutive years. Aside from his recording career, Farnham as an actor performed on stage with lead roles in Australian productions of ''[[Charlie Girl]]'', ''[[Pippin (musical)|Pippin]]'' and 1992's ''[[Jesus Christ Superstar]]''. He starred in his own TV series and specials, including ''It's Magic'' (with [[Colleen Hewett]]), ''[[Bobby Dazzler]]'', and ''Farnham and Byrne'' (with [[Debra Byrne]]), and as a guest on numerous other popular shows ''[[The Don Lane Show]]'', ''[[Countdown (Australian TV series)|Countdown]]'' and ''[[Hey Hey It's Saturday]]''. In August 2022, a cancerous tumour was discovered in Farnham's mouth, which was removed in an operation involving jaw reconstruction. In May 2026 Farnham issued a statement, "because of the surgeries to my mouth and face over the past few years, singing on stage is not something I can consider again".
